analysis.title: APAC Tech: Semiconductors Memory: Kioxia CY3Q26 read-across; mid- to long-term positive NAND outlook intact; Buy SEC/Hynix
key_insights: Kioxia reported CY3Q26 (FY2Q26) results on October 30. GS uses them as a read-across to Samsung Electronics (SEC, Buy on Conviction List) and SK Hynix (Buy).
Kioxia's USD blended ASP rose by mid-20% qoq in CY3Q26, with like-for-like pricing up by low-30%. Bit shipments rose by low-teens, driven by data center and enterprise demand.
Kioxia guides CY4Q26 revenue to slight qoq growth, with bit shipments broadly flat and ASP up modestly. Longer-lead-time products, including data center and enterprise SSDs, shift into CY1Q27.
Kioxia's CY4Q26 guidance is generally below GS expectations for SEC and Hynix. GS attributes the gap to the shipment timing shift and to Kioxia's higher CY3Q26 base relative to the Korean suppliers.

Kioxia expects NAND supply/demand to stay tight through CY27, supported by data center and enterprise demand, leaving room for further ASP increases. Management expects the pace of increases to moderate after the sharp rise from early to mid-CY26 and sees no signs of an ASP decline.
GS expects NAND pricing to rise 34% (SEC) and 30% (Hynix) yoy in CY27E, a slowdown from +279% and +254% in CY26.

Kioxia's CY27 capacity is effectively sold out, and more than 50% of its CY28 shipment volume is already secured under multi-year long-term agreements (LTAs). It is still deciding whether to lock in the rest of CY28 or keep some capacity to capture upside.

Kioxia has begun LTA discussions with customers for CY29-30. GS reads this as a growing chance of a prolonged supply shortage, consistent with SEC and Hynix customers signing five-year LTAs and asking for longer terms.
GS Exhibit 1 puts operating margins for CY3Q26 and CY4Q26E at 68% and 68% for SEC NAND, 72% and 73% for Hynix NAND, and 80% and 80% for Kioxia. Kioxia's CY4Q26E is based on company guidance.
GS valuation anchors: SEC common target W500,000 (EV/EBITDA-based SOTP) and preference share W380,000. Hynix target is W3,500,000 on a 7.0X average 2026E/27E P/E.

market_movers.rationale: Samsung Electronics is Buy on the Conviction List. GS sees Kioxia's results and tight NAND supply/demand through CY27 as consistent with its NAND pricing view for SEC.
SK Hynix is Buy. GS expects NAND pricing up 30% yoy in CY27E and sees five-year LTAs with customers supporting demand visibility.
Kioxia is Buy, covered by Shuhei Nakamura. CY3Q26 ASP and shipments were solid, CY27 is sold out and over 50% of CY28 volume is under LTAs.

sector_views.rationale: GS describes the mid- to long-term NAND outlook as intact, with tight supply/demand through CY27 and multi-year LTAs giving demand visibility beyond CY27-28.

earnings_insights: Kioxia CY3Q26 (FY2Q26), reported 10/30: USD blended ASP up mid-20% qoq, like-for-like pricing up low-30%, bit shipments up low-teens. GS Exhibit 1 shows Kioxia revenue +39% qoq and operating margin 80%.
Kioxia CY4Q26 company guidance (a guide, not a print): revenue slightly up qoq, bit shipments broadly flat, ASP up modestly. GS Exhibit 1 shows revenue +3% qoq and operating margin 80%.
GS estimates for SEC NAND (Exhibit 1, USD): CY3Q26 ASP +17% qoq, bits +4%, revenue +22%, OPM 68%. CY4Q26E is ASP +10%, bits +14%, revenue +25%, OPM 68%.
GS estimates for Hynix NAND (Exhibit 1, USD): CY3Q26 ASP +26% qoq, bits -1%, revenue +26%, OPM 72%. CY4Q26E is ASP +7%, bits +6%, revenue +14%, OPM 73%.
GS says Kioxia's CY4Q26 guidance is generally below its estimates for SEC and Hynix, and links this to shipment timing and the high CY3Q26 base.
risk_factors: SEC: major deterioration in memory supply/demand, sharp contraction in smartphone margins, and mobile OLED market share loss.

Hynix: major deterioration in memory supply/demand and delay in technology migration, weaker smartphone/PC/server demand, Samsung's positive HBM progress affecting Hynix HBM revenue and profit, and lower AI-related capex reducing HBM demand.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 tabulates qoq ASP, bit shipment and revenue growth and operating margin for SEC NAND, Hynix NAND and Kioxia from CY1Q24 to CY4Q26E. Kioxia's operating margin goes from 27% in CY4Q25 to 60%, 74% and 80% in CY1Q26 to CY3Q26, with CY4Q26E (company guidance) at 80%.

tension_points.bull_case: Kioxia expects NAND supply/demand to stay tight through CY27 with no signs of an ASP decline. CY27 is sold out, over 50% of CY28 is under LTAs, and GS expects NAND pricing up 34%/30% yoy for SEC/Hynix in CY27E.
tension_points.bear_case: Kioxia's CY4Q26 guide (flat bits, modest ASP rise) is generally below GS expectations for SEC and Hynix, and management expects the pace of price increases to moderate after the sharp rise in early to mid-CY26. GS attributes the gap to shipment timing and base effects.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Major deterioration in memory supply/demand, which GS lists as the first key downside risk for both SEC and Hynix.

theme_stances.key_argument: Kioxia's results and commentary on data center and enterprise demand support GS's view of tight NAND supply/demand and further pricing upside through CY27.
theme_stances.evidence: Expect NAND S/D to remain tight through CY27, providing further upside to pricing

theme_stances.key_argument: LTA discussions extending to CY29-30 signal a growing chance of a prolonged supply shortage.
theme_stances.evidence: customers are entering into five-year LTAs and asking for even longer period of supply
